statements.markdown: The scalar Gaussian construction is not itself an algorithm on the matrix of SK couplings. A finite-disorder algorithm is obtained by importing the theorem of El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke. In their cited preprint, Assumption 2 asks for a strictly increasing minimizer of the zero-temperature Parisi functional on $\mathcal U$. The support theorem gives this property, and the imported attainment argument supplies the minimizer. Their Corollary 2.2 then returns, for each fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a randomized spin configuration within $\varepsilon n$ of the finite-instance maximum with probability tending to one. Its operation count is the one in the displayed Theorem 3 on p. 7; the preprint's running references call that result “Theorem 3.2.” [El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke, arXiv:2001.00904v1, pp. 7–8][eams20].

The imported operation count is
$C(\varepsilon)(\chi+n)+n\chi_1$, where $\chi$ is the cost of evaluating the full gradient and $\chi_1$ is the cost of one coordinate of the distinct-index gradient. Here $\nabla\widehat H_n(x)=Ax$ costs $O(n^2)$, and one coordinate of $\nabla H_n(x)$ costs $O(n)$. The resulting count is $C(\varepsilon)n^2$, with $C(\varepsilon)$ independent of $n$. Real sums and multiplications have unit cost in the cited model; the scalar functions and normalizers prescribed for the chosen accuracy are part of that construction. This statement supplies neither a bound for their numerical preprocessing nor a finite-precision bit-complexity bound.

Full support and existence give an attained, strictly increasing
minimiser in the monotone zero-temperature class. This is Assumption 2 of
[El Alaoui, Montanari and Sellke, preprint v1][EAMS]. Their Corollary 2.2
then gives, for every fixed $\varepsilon>0$, a randomised algorithm
returning a configuration within $\varepsilon n$ of the finite SK
maximum with probability tending to one over couplings and algorithmic
randomness. Its cost is $C(\varepsilon)n^2$ real-arithmetic operations
with the prescribed scalar functions and normalisers available; this
includes no separate numerical-preprocessing or finite-precision bound.
It does not supply an efficient construction of QAOA angles, a quantum depth bound, or a clause of either selected Lean interface.
